metadata.case_name: HONG KONG RED CROSS v. THE HONG KONG FEDERATION OF YOUTH GROUPS

plaintiff.occupation_before: teacher at the Hong Kong Red Cross Hospital School

source: X-ray of the lumbascaral region did not show any fractures, his diagnosis was ‘back contussion’ and Miss Chan was given analgesic and sent home.
injuries.icd_description: Contusion of lower back or pelvis

source: These findings were consistent with back sprain.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of lumbar spine

manifestations.description: Local tenderness over 4th and 5th lumber regions
only mildly positive straight leg raising tests
persistent low back pain (recurrent, sometimes daily or once every two to three days)
intolerant to prolonged walking, sitting or standing (maximum duration 10-15 minutes)
had to rely on the wheelchair for outdoor activities during periods of exacerbation
presence of muscle guarding and mild spasm over the lumbar region and tenderness over both iliac crests and midline of the lumbar spine particularly over the lumbosacral junction
unable to return to her pre-accident occupation as a teacher of sick children at the hospital

treatments_received: back fitness and physical rehabilitation program

losses.description: Whole person impairment of 5% and persistent low back pain; judge accepted Dr Lam's assessment of 5% whole person impairment and suggested PSLA in the region of $300,000 to $350,000.
Intolerance to prolonged walking, sitting or standing (maximum 10-15 minutes) and reliance on wheelchair for outdoor activities during exacerbations.

Unable to return to pre-accident job as a teacher of sick children at the hospital; loss of earning capacity assessed in the region of 6%; pre-trial loss of earnings for 27.75 months at pre-accident salary $22,683.73 totalling $629,462 and further notional difference to trial of $640,500 (3 Nov 2004 to 3 Dec 2009).
